"""Drill-down tools for the agents (WP1.9). Each tool takes validated arguments, returns compact
rows with evidence references, and is logged as an audit event so that agent citations can be
traced back to the call that produced them.

``TOOLS`` maps a tool name to (argument model, function, description); ``tool_schemas()`` gives
the JSON schemas an LLM needs and ``call_tool`` is the single entry point an agent loop uses.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from sqlalchemy import func, select, text
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from tracepoint.agent.context_pack import build_context_pack
from tracepoint.api import app as api
from tracepoint.core.audit import record_event
from tracepoint.db.models import (
    Finding,
    TaxonomyLevel2,
    TaxonomyLevel3,
    Verbatim,
    VerbatimClassification,
)

Vehicle = Literal["F70", "G60", "G68", "G70"]
MarketCode = Literal["EU", "US", "CN", "RoW"]
FeedbackType = Literal["Likes", "Difficult to Use", "Defect", "Wants"]


def _compact_verbatims(session: Session, rows: list[Verbatim]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    if not rows:
        return []
    l2 = {t.id: t.name for t in session.scalars(select(TaxonomyLevel2))}
    l3 = {t.id: t.name for t in session.scalars(select(TaxonomyLevel3))}
    labels: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for c in session.scalars(
        select(VerbatimClassification).where(
            VerbatimClassification.verbatim_id.in_([v.id for v in rows]),
            VerbatimClassification.status == "canonical",
        )
    ):
        labels.setdefault(c.verbatim_id, []).append(
            f"{c.feedback_type} | {l2.get(c.level2_id)} | {l3.get(c.level3_id)}"
        )
    return [
        {
            "evidence_ref": f"verbatim:{v.id}",
            "market": v.market_code,
            "country": v.country_code,
            "powertrain": v.powertrain,
            "source": v.source_label,
            "text": v.text if v.char_len <= 600 else v.text[:600] + " …",
            "labels": labels.get(v.id, []),
        }
        for v in rows
    ]


# ---- tools -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class SearchEvidenceArgs(BaseModel):
    query: str = Field(description="Free text, e.g. 'charging port flap stuck in cold weather'")
    vehicle: Vehicle | None = None
    market: MarketCode | None = None
    powertrain: str | None = Field(None, description="e.g. BEV, PHEV, ICE")
    feedback_type: FeedbackType | None = None
    domain: str | None = Field(None, description="Vehicle domain key, e.g. interior_comfort")
    limit: int = Field(10, ge=1, le=50)


def search_evidence(session: Session, a: SearchEvidenceArgs) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Ranked full-text search over verbatims with SQL filters."""
    # ponytail: lexical ranking (PostgreSQL full-text, GIN index); add embedding similarity
    # here once the embedding model is named (D-020), the arguments stay the same.
    tsq = func.websearch_to_tsquery("english", a.query)
    vec = func.to_tsvector(text("'english'"), Verbatim.text)
    stmt = select(Verbatim).where(vec.op("@@")(tsq))
    for col, val in (
        (Verbatim.vehicle_code, a.vehicle),
        (Verbatim.market_code, a.market),
        (Verbatim.powertrain, a.powertrain),
    ):
        if val:
            stmt = stmt.where(col == val)
    if a.feedback_type or a.domain:
        sub = select(VerbatimClassification.verbatim_id).where(
            VerbatimClassification.status == "canonical"
        )
        if a.feedback_type:
            sub = sub.where(VerbatimClassification.feedback_type == a.feedback_type)
        if a.domain:
            sub = sub.join(TaxonomyLevel2, TaxonomyLevel2.id == VerbatimClassification.level2_id)
            sub = sub.where(TaxonomyLevel2.domain_key == a.domain)
        stmt = stmt.where(Verbatim.id.in_(sub))
    total = session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(stmt.subquery()))
    rows = session.scalars(
        stmt.order_by(func.ts_rank(vec, tsq).desc(), Verbatim.id).limit(a.limit)
    ).all()
    return {"total": total, "items": _compact_verbatims(session, list(rows))}


class VerbatimsByThemeArgs(BaseModel):
    vehicle: Vehicle
    theme: str = Field(description="Exact level-2 theme name, e.g. 'Electric Range'")
    market: MarketCode | None = None
    feedback_type: FeedbackType | None = None
    limit: int = Field(20, ge=1, le=100)


def get_verbatims_by_theme(session: Session, a: VerbatimsByThemeArgs) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Verbatims carrying a canonical label of one level-2 theme."""
    theme = session.scalar(
        select(TaxonomyLevel2).where(func.lower(TaxonomyLevel2.name) == a.theme.lower())
    )
    if theme is None:
        return {"error": f"unknown theme {a.theme!r}; use the names from the context pack"}
    sub = select(VerbatimClassification.verbatim_id).where(
        VerbatimClassification.level2_id == theme.id, VerbatimClassification.status == "canonical"
    )
    if a.feedback_type:
        sub = sub.where(VerbatimClassification.feedback_type == a.feedback_type)
    stmt = select(Verbatim).where(Verbatim.vehicle_code == a.vehicle, Verbatim.id.in_(sub))
    if a.market:
        stmt = stmt.where(Verbatim.market_code == a.market)
    total = session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(stmt.subquery()))
    rows = session.scalars(stmt.order_by(Verbatim.id).limit(a.limit)).all()
    return {"theme": theme.name, "domain": theme.domain_key, "total": total,
            "items": _compact_verbatims(session, list(rows))}


class MetricArgs(BaseModel):
    vehicle: Vehicle
    market: MarketCode | None = None
    attribute: str | None = Field(None, description="Substring of the study attribute name")
    domain: str | None = None


def get_metric(session: Session, a: MetricArgs) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Customer-study metrics (means or distributions) with evidence references."""
    rows = api.studies(vehicle=a.vehicle, market=a.market, study=None, session=session)
    rows = [
        {k: r[k] for k in ("evidence_ref", "market_code", "study", "attribute_raw", "domain_key",
                           "stat_kind", "mean", "distribution", "scale_note")}
        for r in rows
        if (not a.attribute or a.attribute.lower() in r["attribute_raw"].lower())
        and (not a.domain or r["domain_key"] == a.domain)
    ]
    return {"total": len(rows), "items": rows}


class EquipmentArgs(BaseModel):
    vehicle: Vehicle
    query: str | None = Field(None, description="Substring of the German or English item name")
    group: str | None = None
    domain: str | None = None
    limit: int = Field(30, ge=1, le=200)


def get_equipment(session: Session, a: EquipmentArgs) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Catalogue items with price and standard / optional / not-available status per variant."""
    rows = api.equipment(vehicle=a.vehicle, group=a.group, q=a.query, session=session)
    rows = [
        {k: r[k] for k in ("evidence_ref", "sa_code", "name_en", "group_key", "domain_key",
                           "price_eur", "availability")}
        for r in rows
        if not a.domain or r["domain_key"] == a.domain
    ]
    return {"total": len(rows), "items": rows[: a.limit]}


class SalesArgs(BaseModel):
    vehicle: Vehicle
    market: MarketCode | None = None


def get_sales(session: Session, a: SalesArgs) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Sales volumes per market and year (2030 is a plan figure)."""
    rows = api.sales(vehicle=a.vehicle, session=session)
    rows = [
        {k: r[k] for k in ("evidence_ref", "market_code", "year", "units", "kind", "note")}
        for r in rows
        if not a.market or r["market_code"] == a.market
    ]
    return {"total": len(rows), "items": rows}


class FindingsArgs(BaseModel):
    vehicle: Vehicle
    market: MarketCode | None = None
    domain: str | None = None
    kind: str | None = Field(None, description="e.g. recurring_complaint, unmet_need, metric_gap")
    limit: int = Field(20, ge=1, le=100)


def get_findings(session: Session, a: FindingsArgs) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Extracted findings; drill into one with the API route /findings/{id} for its evidence."""
    stmt = select(Finding).where(Finding.vehicle_code == a.vehicle, Finding.status != "withdrawn")
    for col, val in ((Finding.market_code, a.market), (Finding.domain_key, a.domain),
                     (Finding.kind, a.kind)):
        if val:
            stmt = stmt.where(col == val)
    rows = session.scalars(
        stmt.order_by(Finding.evidence_level, Finding.severity_score.desc().nulls_last())
        .limit(a.limit)
    ).all()
    return {"items": [
        {"id": f.id, "kind": f.kind, "layer": f.layer, "domain": f.domain_key, "title": f.title,
         "statement": f.statement, "evidence_level": f.evidence_level,
         "evidence_count": f.evidence_count, "quantification": f.quantification}
        for f in rows
    ]}


class ContextPackArgs(BaseModel):
    vehicle: Vehicle
    market: MarketCode | None = None


def get_context_pack(session: Session, a: ContextPackArgs) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Compact overview of one vehicle × market; the starting point before drilling down."""
    return build_context_pack(session, a.vehicle, a.market)


TOOLS: dict[str, tuple[type[BaseModel], Callable[[Session, Any], dict[str, Any]]]] = {
    "get_context_pack": (ContextPackArgs, get_context_pack),
    "search_evidence": (SearchEvidenceArgs, search_evidence),
    "get_verbatims_by_theme": (VerbatimsByThemeArgs, get_verbatims_by_theme),
    "get_metric": (MetricArgs, get_metric),
    "get_equipment": (EquipmentArgs, get_equipment),
    "get_sales": (SalesArgs, get_sales),
    "get_findings": (FindingsArgs, get_findings),
}


def tool_schemas() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Name, description and JSON input schema per tool (provider-neutral)."""
    return [
        {"name": name, "description": (fn.__doc__ or "").strip(),
         "input_schema": model.model_json_schema()}
        for name, (model, fn) in TOOLS.items()
    ]


def _refs(result: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    return [r["evidence_ref"] for r in result.get("items", []) if "evidence_ref" in r][:50]


def call_tool(
    session: Session,
    name: str,
    args: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    actor_id: str = "agent:unknown",
    run_id: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Validate the arguments, run the tool and log the call. Raises KeyError / ValidationError
    on an unknown tool or bad arguments so the agent loop can report them back to the model."""
    model, fn = TOOLS[name]
    parsed = model.model_validate(args)
    result = fn(session, parsed)
    record_event(
        session,
        actor_type="agent",
        actor_id=actor_id,
        action="tool.called",
        entity_type="tool",
        entity_id=name,
        run_id=run_id,
        after={"args": parsed.model_dump(exclude_none=True), "total": result.get("total"),
               "evidence_refs": _refs(result)},
    )
    session.flush()
    return result

| Status | Done – 38 tests passed, clean rebuild with `./start.sh --reset` verified; embedding similarity still waits for the embedding model (D-020) |
| Why | The ingested and classified evidence has to be usable by the agents of the later phases, following the three access modes of the Phase 1 plan § 3.3 |

## 1. Delivered

`backend/tracepoint/agent/`, decision D-053.

* **Context packs** (`context_pack.py`, version `context-pack-v1`): one compact JSON + Markdown
  summary per vehicle × market with evidence: coverage, the nine domains with complaint share,
  top eight complaint themes and top five strengths with three quotes each, weakest and strongest
  study attributes, variants and equipment optional on every variant, sales by year, the fifteen
  strongest findings. Every quote, metric and item carries its evidence reference. About 18 kB
  JSON / 2,500 tokens of Markdown per pack, built in about 0.25 s, so packs are rebuilt on demand
  instead of cached. `tracepoint agent packs` writes the ten packs with evidence (F70 EU/RoW,
  G60 EU/US/RoW, G68 CN, G70 EU/US/CN/RoW) to `data/context_packs/`; `start.sh` runs it.
* **Drill-down tools** (`tools.py`): `get_context_pack`, `search_evidence`,
  `get_verbatims_by_theme`, `get_metric`, `get_equipment`, `get_sales`, `get_findings`.
  Arguments are Pydantic models (vehicle and market codes are enumerations, limits bounded), so
  model output is validated before it reaches SQL. `tool_schemas()` returns provider-neutral
  name / description / JSON schema triples for the LLM gateway. `call_tool()` is the single entry
  point and writes one audit event (`tool.called`, actor, arguments, total, up to 50 evidence
  references) per call.
* **`search_evidence`** ranks verbatims with PostgreSQL full-text search over the existing GIN
  index (any word may match, length-normalised rank) after SQL filters on vehicle, market,
  powertrain, feedback type and domain. Embedding similarity can later be added inside the same
  function without changing its arguments.
* Access paths: Python (`call_tool`), CLI (`tracepoint agent tools | call | packs`), HTTP
  (`GET /agent/tools`, `POST /agent/tools/{name}`, 404 for unknown tools, 422 for bad arguments).

## 2. Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Ten hand-written retrieval queries (plan acceptance) | all ten return five results with at least four relevant ones in the top five (test `test_search_evidence_top5_relevant`) |
| Context packs for all vehicles | ten packs in under three seconds in total (acceptance: under a minute) |
| Tool calls in the event log | every tool logged with actor and evidence references (test `test_every_tool_runs_and_is_logged`) |
| Bad arguments | rejected by validation (unknown vehicle code → `ValidationError` / HTTP 422) |
| Tests / lint | 38 passed; `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean |

## 3. Known limitations

* Relevance in the retrieval test is checked by key words in the text, not by human judgement.
* Lexical search misses paraphrases ("flap" vs "charge port door" only meet through shared
  words); this is what embeddings will add.
* The tools read; agents cannot write findings or requirements yet (Phase 3 / 4).

## 4. Phase 1 status after this step

Open: blind validation of the classifications (needs an API key), Source B segmentation,
embedding similarity, close-out report WP1.11.

Planın 3.3 bölümündeki agent erişim katmanını, embedding hariç, kurdum. Artık bir AI agent veriye hazır özetler ve araçlar üzerinden ulaşabiliyor. `./start.sh --reset` ile sıfırdan kurulumu tekrar denedim; 38 testin hepsi geçti. Hiçbir şey commit edilmedi.

**1. Context pack (agent'ın başlangıç noktası)**
- Her araç × pazar için kısa bir özet var: domain'lere göre şikâyet ve övgü oranları, en çok şikâyet edilen 8 tema ve en çok övülen 5 tema (her birinde 3 müşteri alıntısı), study'lerdeki en zayıf ve en güçlü attribute'lar, her varyantta opsiyon olan donanımlar, satış rakamları ve en güçlü 15 bulgu.
- Her alıntı ve rakam kaynağını gösteren bir referans taşıyor (`verbatim:G60-0540` gibi). Böylece agent'ın verdiği her bilgi kontrol edilebiliyor.
- Bir pack yaklaşık 2.500 token, yani prompt'a rahatça sığıyor. Üretmesi 0,25 saniye sürüyor.
- 10 pack üretildi: F70 EU/RoW, G60 EU/US/RoW, G68 CN, G70 EU/US/CN/RoW. Dosyalar `data/context_packs/` altında; `start.sh` bunları her kurulumda yeniden üretiyor.

**2. Agent araçları (detaya inmek için)**

| Araç | Ne yapıyor |
|---|---|
| `get_context_pack` | Yukarıdaki özeti döndürüyor |
| `search_evidence` | Serbest metinle arama yapıyor ("şarj kapağı soğukta açılmıyor" gibi); araç, pazar, motor tipi, feedback tipi ve domain filtresi alıyor |
| `get_verbatims_by_theme` | Bir temaya ait müşteri yorumlarını getiriyor |
| `get_metric` | Study skorlarını getiriyor |
| `get_equipment` | Donanım listesini, fiyatı ve her varyanttaki standart/opsiyon/yok durumunu getiriyor |
| `get_sales` | Pazar ve yıl bazında satışları getiriyor |
| `get_findings` | Çıkarılan bulguları getiriyor (planda yoktu; Faz 4'te gereksinim türetmek için lazım olacak) |

- Agent'ın gönderdiği parametreler kontrol ediliyor. Örneğin olmayan bir araç kodu gelirse sorgu çalışmadan reddediliyor.
- Her araç çağrısı audit log'a kaydediliyor: kim çağırdı, hangi parametrelerle, hangi kanıtları aldı.
- Araçlara üç yoldan erişilebiliyor:
  - Python içinden `call_tool()`
  - Komut satırından `tracepoint agent call ...`
  - HTTP üzerinden `GET /agent/tools` ve `POST /agent/tools/{name}`
- `tool_schemas()` araç tanımlarını LLM'in anlayacağı formatta veriyor; OpenAI veya Anthropic'e doğrudan verilebilir.

**Planın kabul kriterleri**
- Elle yazılmış 10 arama sorgusunun hepsinde ilk 5 sonucun en az 4'ü ilgili çıktı. Bunu test olarak ekledim; ilgililik metinde anahtar kelime aranarak ölçülüyor, insan değerlendirmesiyle değil.
- 10 pack'in hepsi toplam 3 saniyenin altında üretiliyor (kriter 1 dakikaydı).
- Araç çağrıları audit log'da görünüyor.

**Eksik kalanlar**
- **Anlamsal arama yok.** Arama şu an kelime eşleşmesiyle çalışıyor (PostgreSQL full-text). Farklı kelimelerle anlatılan aynı şikâyeti kaçırabilir. Embedding modeli seçilince aynı fonksiyonun içine eklenecek; agent tarafında hiçbir şey değişmeyecek.
- **Faz 1'de hâlâ açık olanlar:** etiketlerin kör doğrulaması (API gerekiyor), Source B segmentasyonu, embedding ve faz kapanış raporu.
- **`start.ps1`'e yaptığım ekleme denenmedi**, çünkü bu makinede PowerShell yok.

Kararı D-053 olarak kaydettim, raporu `reports/step-10-agent-context-packs-and-tools.md` dosyasına yazdım, plandaki WP1.7 ve WP1.9 durum satırlarını güncelledim.

Bekleyen iki adımı (gap classification ile bu adım) ayrı branch açıp commit'leyeyim ve PR oluşturayım mı?
vDB nerede lazım olacaktı? yoksa kullanmasak olur mu? objektif ve hackathon odaklı düşün

Kısa cevap: ayrı bir vector DB'ye gerek yok, hackathon için kullanmayın. Plan zaten ayrı bir vector DB öngörmüyordu (D-005, plan bölüm 3.3). Öngörülen şey, Postgres içinde tek bir `embedding` tablosu ve uygulama içinde benzerlik hesabıydı. Asıl soru "embedding'e gerek var mı?" ve onun da cevabı: şimdilik hayır.

**Planda embedding nerede kullanılacaktı, şu an durum ne**

| Kullanım yeri (plan 3.3) | Durum | Embedding şart mı? |
|---|---|---|
| Gap classification için benzer örnek bulma | İş bitti. Örnekler kelime aramasıyla bulunuyor (D-034) | Hayır |
| Tekrar sayımı ("kaç kişi menzilden şikâyet ediyor") | SQL ve taksonomi ile çözülüyor; plan da embedding istemiyordu | Hayır |
| PM'in "challenge" araması (serbest metinle kanıt arama) | Kelime araması 10/10 testi geçti. Zayıf noktası eş anlamlılar ("flap" ile "charge port door") | Kısmen |
| Katmanlar arası bağlantı (tema ↔ study attribute ↔ donanım) | Şu an elle yazılmış YAML eşlemeleriyle yapılıyor | Hayır; LLM'e eşleme önerdirmek daha ucuz |
| Faz 2: rakip araç yorumlarını bizim temalarla eşleştirmek | Henüz yok | En güçlü aday, ama LLM'e tema etiketlettirmek de çözer (gap classification ile aynı yol) |
| Faz 4: tekrar eden gereksinimleri birleştirmek | Henüz yok | Hayır; en fazla ~100 gereksinim tek bir prompt'a sığar |

**Neden gerek yok**
- **Veri küçük.** Yaklaşık 15 bin metin var (verbatim, segment, donanım, metrik). Bunların hepsinin embedding'i belleğe sığar (1536 boyutta yaklaşık 90 MB). Numpy ile benzerlik hesabı milisaniyeler sürer. Bu ölçekte indeks gerektiren bir vector DB fayda sağlamaz.
- **Asıl sinyal zaten etiketlerde.** Verbatim'lerin tamamı taksonomiyle etiketli. Agent "temaya göre getir" ve SQL toplamlarıyla daha doğru ve açıklanabilir sonuç alıyor. Jüriye "bu sayı şu satırlardan geliyor" diyebilmek, "benzerlik skoru 0,82" demekten daha ikna edici. İzlenebilirlik zaten projenin ana iddiası.
- **Her ek parça demoda bir risk.** pgvector farklı bir Postgres imajı ister, embedding modeli ve API anahtarı gerektirir, her yeni veride embedding'lerin yeniden hesaplanması gerekir. Bunlar ekip arkadaşlarının makinesinde `./start.sh`'in bozulma ihtimalini artırır.

**Eş anlamlı sorunu için ucuz çözüm**
- Agent arama yapmadan önce sorguyu kendisi genişletir: "charging flap stuck" → "charging flap port door cover stuck open". Bu sadece agent'ın system prompt'una bir cümle eklemek demek, kod gerekmiyor. Anlamsal aramanın sağlayacağı kazancın çoğunu bu karşılar.

**Ne zaman fikrimi değiştiririm**
- Faz 2'de etiketsiz binlerce dış kaynak metin gelirse ve LLM ile etiketlemek pahalı ya da yavaş kalırsa.
- Demoda "serbest soru sor, anlamca en yakın kanıt gelsin" özelliği jüriye gösterilecek ana an olarak seçilirse.

Bu durumda bile ayrı bir servis kurmam. Embedding'leri mevcut Postgres'e bir tablo olarak eklerim, benzerliği `search_evidence` fonksiyonunun içinde hesaplarım. Agent'ın kullandığı araçlar değişmez. Embedding maliyeti yaklaşık 1 milyon token, birkaç cent tutar.

**Önerim:** embedding'i ertelemek ve planın 13. bölümündeki açık maddeyi (3. madde: "pgvector kurulsun mu?") "hayır, ihtiyaç doğarsa Postgres tablosu ve uygulama içi hesap" diye kapatmak. Bunu karar kaydına D-054 olarak yazayım mı?

## 5. End-to-end workflow and human gates (deliverable D3)

| Step | Activity | Actor |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Register sources; ingest internal files; fill classification gaps; translate; embed | AI (autonomous) |
| 2 | Fetch team-selected external sources; cache; extract evidence | AI (autonomous); source list by humans |
| 3 | Extract findings per layer; link across layers; assign evidence levels | AI (autonomous) |
| **G1** | **Approve the finding / theme set** (including new taxonomy proposals) | **PM (mandatory)** |
| 4 | Derive candidate requirements (implement? 0/1); specify approved candidates with measurable, region-specific acceptance criteria, horizon, assumptions | AI (autonomous) |
| **G2** | **Approve / reject / edit each requirement before it enters the prioritised backlog** | **PM (mandatory)** |
| 5 | Propose weight profile; score; build variations with rough effort / cost; produce report version | AI (proposes) |
| **G3** | **Approve the weight profile and the resulting priorities; any weight change → deterministic re-run → report diff → PM accepts** | **PM (mandatory)** |
| 6 | PM decides per vehicle domain and horizon (approve now, defer to H2, reject); challenges trigger logged re-analysis | PM + AI on demand |
| **G4** | **Release the requirement list (versioned)** | **PM (mandatory)** |
| 7 | Audit trail, traceability views, exports | System |

---

## 6. Prioritisation concept (to be detailed in Phase 5)

* **Factor families**, one per layer plus cross-cutting factors: customer impact (frequency ×
  severity, where Defect > Difficult to use > Want; sentiment), metric gap, regional fit,
  competitive pressure, portfolio fit (including tier dampening), trend alignment, evidence
  strength (evidence level), rough effort / cost (negative), horizon feasibility.
* **Weight profiles** per vehicle × market: AI-proposed with written rationale, PM-adjustable,
  versioned. Region profiles encode context such as climate and usage patterns.
* **Deterministic scoring**: score = Σ (weight × normalised factor) with every component and
  reason stored; a weight change re-scores stored findings without re-fetching and produces a new
  report version plus a diff against the previous one.
* **Variations**: scenario runs (evolve existing model / new generation / split by domain) with
  rough effort and cost estimates and expected customer impact; the AI reports pros, cons and
  suggestions; the PM chooses per domain.
* **Evidence levels**: A = multiple independent sources and quantitative confirmation; B = several
  items from one source family; C = single or weak item, or web-only; D = assumption. Definitions
  will be tuned in Phase 3.

---

## 7. Phases

### 7.1 Overview

| # | Phase | Goal | Main outputs | Deliverable mapping |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Foundation and internal evidence base** (active; internal ingestion delivered in step 03) | Working skeleton; all internal files ingested, normalised, classified, translated, embedded; audit log live; baseline reports | Repo skeleton, data model, parsers, canonical taxonomy, classifier, retrieval, API, baseline situation-analysis reports | D1 (foundation), D4 (log core) |
| 2 | External evidence ingestion | Research sub-agents fetch team-selected sources and cache them; structured evidence for layers L1–L4, L6 | Source registry, fetch / snapshot pipeline, extractors, reliability tagging | D1 |
| 3 | Signal extraction and cross-layer linking (first deterministic iteration delivered in step 04) | Findings per layer with quantification, evidence levels and links | Finding agents, linker, finding store, G1 queue | D2 (findings) |
| 4 | Requirement derivation and specification | Candidate 0/1 step; specified requirements with region-specific acceptance criteria, horizon, assumptions | Requirement agent, scope filter, consolidation, G2 queue | D2 |
| 5 | Prioritisation engine, variations and estimation | Explainable, adjustable scoring; variations with rough effort / cost; report versions and diffs | Scoring engine, weight-proposal agent, estimation / variation agent, compare | D2 |
| 6 | PM workspace | Review queue, gates G1–G4, edit / defer per domain and horizon, challenge flow, weight tuning and comparison, traceability view | Web UI + API | D1, D3 |
| 7 | Audit trail completion and exports | Completeness check of the trail; traceability views; exports of the requirement list and the event log | Exports (JSON / CSV / XLSX), traceability report | D2, D4 |
| 8 | Adaptability, hardening and demo mode | Second derivative / market run; cache-only demo mode; pitch material | Config for second vehicle, demo script, presentation | D1–D4 |

Cross-cutting (every phase): step reports and pull requests, tests and data-quality checks,
configuration over code, cost and token tracking of LLM calls, security of keys and secrets.

### 7.2 Phase details

**Phase 1 – Foundation and internal evidence base.** See the dedicated plan. Exit criteria: one
command ingests all eight internal files reproducibly with counts verified against step 01;
every evidence item has a locator; canonical taxonomy with domain mapping; unclassified verbatims
classified with confidence and new-theme proposals queued; equipment matrix translated and
queryable; retrieval works with filters; every ingestion and classification is in the event log
and exportable; baseline reports per vehicle generated; tests pass in CI.

**Phase 2 – External evidence ingestion.** Inputs: the team's source list (competitor products
and their customer feedback, regional statistics, magazines, trend reports; for example a Chinese
competitor's comparable car). Activities: source registry with layer, reliability and licence
notes; research sub-agents using server-side web search / fetch restricted to allowed domains;
snapshot cache (raw page, fetch time, checksum) in the database; extractors producing evidence
items with locators (URL + excerpt); deduplication; cache-only mode for the pitch. Exit criteria:
every external evidence item is reproducible from its cached snapshot; the pipeline runs offline
from the cache.

**Phase 3 – Signal extraction and cross-layer linking.** Activities: finding agents per layer
(VoC recurrence and severity per vehicle × market × powertrain, metric gaps, equipment gaps,
competitor advantages, regional expectations, trends, portfolio constraints); evidence-level
assignment; linker producing cross-layer links with rationale; G1 queue (finding set + taxonomy
proposals). Exit criteria: every finding has quantified evidence, a level and links; the PM can
approve the finding set.

**Phase 4 – Requirement derivation and specification.** Activities: candidate generation with
0/1 "implement?" proposal and reasons; scope classifier (in / out of the challenge scope);
specification with measurable, region-specific acceptance criteria (for example "rear-seat
screens available in CN variants", "cabin pre-heating time ≤ X minutes at −15 °C for Nordic
markets"), horizon H1 / H2 with reason, assumptions and uncertainties; consolidation and
deduplication; G2 queue. Exit criteria: a structured requirement list for the demo vehicle with
every mandatory field of deliverable D2.

**Phase 5 – Prioritisation engine, variations and estimation.** Activities: factor computation
per layer; AI weight-profile proposal with rationale; deterministic scoring with stored
components; portfolio tier dampening and regional modifiers with visible reasons; rough effort /
cost estimation (T-shirt sizes, reasons, uncertainty); variations (evolve existing / new
generation / split by domain); report versions and diffs; G3 queue. Exit criteria: a change of
weights re-scores without re-fetching and produces a comparable report.

**Phase 6 – PM workspace.** Activities: web UI for the review queue, gates G1–G4, edit with
versioning, decide per vehicle domain and horizon (approve / reject / defer), challenge flow with
logged AI re-analysis, weight editor with re-run and comparison, traceability view (requirement →
findings → evidence → sources), event timeline per requirement. Exit criteria: the complete
workflow of section 5 can be executed in the UI by one PM.

**Phase 7 – Audit trail completion and exports.** Activities: completeness audit (every
change to content, score, priority, evidence or status has an event with actor, time and
rationale); exports of the event log and the requirement list (JSON, CSV, XLSX); traceability
report generator. Exit criteria: deliverables D2 and D4 are exportable from the application.

**Phase 8 – Adaptability, hardening and demo mode.** Activities: run the full pipeline for a
second derivative and market by configuration only; cache-only demo mode; performance and
robustness fixes; pitch material and demo script (the demo itself is decided after the project
is complete). Exit criteria: second vehicle run succeeds without code changes to the pipeline.

---

## 8. Deliverable traceability

| Deliverable | Where it is produced |
|---|---|
| D1 Concept + demonstrable prototype | Phases 1–6 (prototype), this plan (concept) |
| D2 Structured requirement list with all mandatory fields | Phases 3–5 (content), Phase 7 (export) |
| D3 End-to-end workflow with autonomy map and mandatory human review | Section 5 of this plan, refined in Phases 4–6 |
| D4 Demonstrable audit trail | Phase 1 (event log core), every phase (events), Phase 7 (views and exports) |

---

## 9. Conventions

* **Language:** English for code, documentation, commit messages, UI and reports.
* **Repository layout:** `docs/` raw challenge inputs (read-only) · `plan/` master plan, phase
  plans, decision log · `reports/` step reports (`step-NN-<topic>.md`) · `config/` profiles,
  taxonomy, sources, weights · `backend/` Python application · `frontend/` web UI (from Phase 6,
  optionally a minimal explorer earlier) · `data/` generated artefacts (database, caches, exports;
  git-ignored except small samples).
* **Branching:** work on the designated branch, one pull request per step to `main`; the team
  merges.
* **Reporting:** every step produces a report before its pull request; the report states what was
  done, what was verified (with numbers), what was decided and what is next.
* **Decisions:** recorded in `plan/decisions.md` with an ID, date, context and consequences.
* **Configuration over code:** vehicle, market, portfolio and weight profiles, taxonomy mappings
  and the source registry are files under `config/`.

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Evidence source** | A registered origin of evidence: an internal file (sheet, PDF) or an external web page / document fetched by a research agent. Has a kind, a layer, a reliability note and a fetch timestamp. |
| **Evidence item** | The atomic, addressable unit of evidence: a verbatim, a classification row, a study metric, a sales figure, an equipment line, a technical value, a web excerpt. Every item has a **locator**. |
| **Evidence layer** | One of six lenses through which evidence is grouped and scored: Voice of Customer, Quantitative Metrics, Regional Demand & Context, Competition, Portfolio & Offering, Market Trends (section 4.2). |
| **Vehicle domain** | The part of the car a requirement changes; the unit at which the PM can decide and defer: Exterior & Design, Interior Comfort & Materials, Space & Practicality, Infotainment & Digital Services, Driver Assistance & Parking, Powertrain Range & Charging (as experienced), Driving Experience & Dynamics, Quality Perception & NVH, Variant & Package Offering; plus General for cross-cutting statements (`config/taxonomy/domains.yaml`). |
| **Finding** | A layer-specific, quantified signal with linked evidence: recurring complaint, unmet need, strength to keep, metric gap, equipment gap, competitor advantage, regional expectation, trend, portfolio constraint. Has an evidence level. |
| **Finding link** | A cross-layer connection between findings (supports / contradicts / explains) with a written rationale. |
| **Requirement** | A customer-facing, actionable statement derived from findings, with ID, vehicle domain, horizon, region applicability, measurable acceptance criteria per region, rationale, assumptions and uncertainties, evidence level, status, versions. |
| **Horizon** | **H1 near-term**: achievable within the current generation (model-year update, LCI, software / OTA, equipment, packages, colours, trims; roughly within two years). **H2 long-term**: successor generation (about 2030 and later, matching the 2030 sales forecast). |
| **Weight profile** | The set of factor and layer weights used for scoring for a given vehicle and market. AI-proposed with rationale, PM-adjustable, versioned. |
| **Priority score** | A deterministic score computed from findings, profiles and weights, shown as components plus total plus written rationale. |
| **Variation (scenario)** | An alternative allocation of requirements to horizons / vehicle domains (for example "evolve the current car" vs "carry into the new generation" vs "split by domain") with rough effort and cost estimates and expected customer impact. |
| **Gate** | A mandatory PM decision point (section 5). |
| **Challenge** | A PM question or dispute about a requirement, its evidence or its score; triggers a logged AI re-analysis (for example "re-score without source B", "is this still valid for BEV?"). |
| **Audit event** | An append-only record: timestamp, actor (human / agent / system), action, entity, before / after, rationale, run, model and prompt version where applicable. |
| **Run** | One execution of a pipeline stage with a configuration snapshot, code version and model identifiers; all events and outputs reference their run. |

---

Gereksinim türetmeyi planlara (master plan Faz 4, D2, D-008, D-009, D-013) ve elimizdeki gerçek veriye göre detaylandırdım.

## Ne üretiyoruz

Gereksinim, bulgulardan türetilen ve müşteriye dönük, uygulanabilir bir ifade. Bulgu "ne sorun var"ı söyler, gereksinim "araç ne yapmalı"yı. Örnek:

- **Bulgu:** `FND-G60-US-VOC-seats`. G60 US'te koltuk konforu en çok şikâyet edilen interior teması (kanıt seviyesi A, severity 129), zayıf seat-comfort study skorlarıyla destekleniyor.
- **Gereksinim:**
  - `REQ-G60-IC-003` "Sürücü koltuğu, 1,60–1,90 m boyundaki sürücülere 2 saatlik sürüşte bel ağrısı yapmayacak şekilde ayarlanabilmeli; bel desteği tamamen düzleştirilebilmeli."
  - Kabul kriterleri: US'te study'deki seat comfort skoru ≥ segment ortalaması; koltuk şikâyet oranı < %X.
  - Ufuk H1 (yazılım ve donanım güncellemesiyle yapılabilir).

## D2'nin zorunlu alanları nasıl doluyor

| D2 alanı (step 01) | Gereksinimdeki karşılığı | Kaynağı |
|---|---|---|
| Benzersiz ID | `REQ-<araç>-<domain>-<no>`, kalıcı | Kod |
| Açık, uygulanabilir tanım | `title` ve `statement` | Agent |
| Bağlı bulgular ve kaynaklar | Bulgu ID'leri; kaynaklara bulgular üzerinden zaten ulaşılıyor | Agent seçer, kod doğrular |
| Öncelik veya skor | Faz 5'te deterministik hesaplanacak | Kod |
| Önceliklendirme gerekçesi | Skor bileşenleri ve yazılı gerekçe | Faz 5 |
| Kanıt seviyesi | Bağlı bulguların en güçlüsünden hesaplanıyor (A–D) | Kod |
| Varsayımlar ve belirsizlikler | `assumptions`, `uncertainties` listeleri (örneğin D-015 motor dağılımı varsayımı) | Agent |
| Güncel karar durumu | proposed → approved / rejected / deferred-H2 | PM (G2 gate) |

Planın ek istedikleri: domain (karar ve erteleme birimi, D-012), ufuk H1/H2 ve gerekçesi (D-008), pazar bazında kabul kriterleri (D-013), versiyon ve tüm değişikliklerin audit event'i.

## Akış (master plan bölüm 5, adım 4 ve G2)

1. **Aday üretme.** Agent her güçlü bulgu kümesine bakıp "uygulansın mı?" (0/1) önerisini gerekçesiyle verir. "Strength" türü bulgular "korunacak özellik" gereksinimine dönüşebilir; kanıtı zayıf (D seviyesi) olanlar elenir.
2. **Kapsam filtresi.** Bayi, finansman, servis süreci, fiyat pazarlığı ve mühendislik detayı kapsam dışı. Gerekçesiyle elenir ve bu da loglanır.
3. **Spesifikasyon.** Ölçülebilir kabul kriterleri, pazara göre farklılaşma (örneğin kış menzili CN/EU'da farklı hedeflerle), ufuk, varsayımlar.
4. **Birleştirme.** Aynı ihtiyaç birden fazla bulgudan geliyorsa tek gereksinimde toplanır. Örneğin "fiziksel klima düğmesi" hem F70 EU'da hem G60 US'te var; araç bazında ayrı tutulup birbirine bağlanır.
5. **G2 gate.** PM her gereksinimi onaylar, reddeder, düzenler veya H2'ye erteler. UI gelene kadar bu işlem API ve CLI üzerinden yapılır, her karar audit log'a yazılır.

## Uygulama (gap classification ile aynı desen)

- **Veri modeli:** `requirement`, `requirement_finding` (bağlantı ve rolü: "primary"/"supporting"), `requirement_criterion` (pazar, metrik, hedef, ölçüm yöntemi) ve versiyon geçmişi.
- **Üretim:** Agent'a o araç ve pazarın context pack'i verilir, araçlarla detaya iner ve sonucu sabit bir şemada döndürür. API anahtarı yokken bu işi ben yaparım: sonuç `config/requirements/<araç>_<pazar>.yaml` dosyasına yazılır ve commit edilir. Anahtar gelince aynı şema OpenAI ile doldurulur; kod değişmez.
- **Kod tarafındaki kontroller:** bağlanan bulgu ID'leri gerçekten var mı, her gereksinimin en az bir A–C seviyesinde bulgusu var mı, kanıt seviyesi hesabı, ID'lerin kalıcılığı, yeniden import edilince sistemin bozulmaması.
- **Çıktılar:** `GET /requirements` (filtreli), `GET /requirements/{id}` (gereksinim → bulgu → kanıt → kaynak zinciri ve event geçmişi), `POST /requirements/{id}/decision` (G2), Markdown ve CSV export (D2 örnek listesi).
- **Tahmini kapsam:** bir step. Bunun yaklaşık yarısı kod, yarısı içerik üretmek.

## Senin karar vermen gereken 3 nokta

1. **Hangi araç × pazar ile başlayalım?** En çok bulgu G60 US (226) ve G70 US'te (269). F70 EU Avrupa tarafını temsil ediyor. Önerim: G60 US, G70 US ve F70 EU. G60 EU'da bulgu az (35), onu sonraya bırakırım.
2. **Kapsam başına kaç gereksinim?** Önerim 12–20. Jüri için okunabilir bir liste olur; az sayıda ama A/B kanıtlı gereksinim, çok sayıda zayıf gereksinimden daha ikna edici.
3. **Kabul kriterlerindeki hedef sayılar.** Elimizde mühendislik verisi yok. Hedefleri iki yerden türetebilirim: study skorları (segment ortalaması ve rakip kıyası) ve şikâyet oranlarındaki düşüş. Kesin olmayan hedefleri "varsayım" diye işaretlerim. Bu yaklaşım uygun mu, yoksa ekip mühendislik hedefi gibi somut değerler mi istiyor?

Bu üç noktada önerdiğim varsayılanlarla başlayabilirim, ya da sen farklı bir şey söyle.
tamam entegre et bi bakalım

Varsayılanlarla başlıyorum: G60 US, G70 US ve F70 EU kapsamları; kapsam başına 12–20 gereksinim; hedefleri study skorlarından ve şikâyet oranlarından türetip varsayım olarak işaretleyeceğim. Önce mevcut model ve versiyonlama desenine bakıyorum.

def extract_findings(
    session: Session, run: Run, vehicle_code: str, market: str | None = None
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    cfg = load_config()
    vehicle = session.get(Vehicle, vehicle_code)
    if vehicle is None:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown vehicle {vehicle_code}")
    if market and session.get(Market, market) is None:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown market {market}")
    l2 = {t.id: t for t in session.scalars(select(TaxonomyLevel2))}
    voc = _voc_drafts(session, cfg, vehicle, market, l2)
    met = _metric_drafts(session, cfg, vehicle, market)
    eq = _equipment_drafts(session, cfg, vehicle, market, voc, l2)
    _link_voc_metrics(cfg, voc, met, l2)
    drafts = voc + met + eq
    stats: Counter = Counter(
        {"created": 0, "updated": 0, "unchanged": 0, "withdrawn": 0, "links": 0}
    )
    ids = [d.id for d in drafts]
    # remove links owned by this extractor for the scope, then re-create
    scope_ids = select(Finding.id).where(
        Finding.vehicle_code == vehicle_code,
        Finding.market_code == market,
        Finding.created_by == ACTOR,
    )
    session.execute(
        delete(FindingLink).where(
            FindingLink.created_by == ACTOR, FindingLink.from_finding_id.in_(scope_ids)
        )
    )
    for d in drafts:
        _upsert(session, run, d, vehicle_code, market, stats)
    # findings of this scope that are no longer produced are withdrawn (kept for the audit trail)
    stale = session.scalars(
        select(Finding).where(
            Finding.vehicle_code == vehicle_code,
            Finding.market_code == market,
            Finding.created_by == ACTOR,
            Finding.status != "withdrawn",
            Finding.id.notin_(ids),
        )
    ).all()
    for f in stale:
        before = {"status": f.status, "version": f.version}
        f.status = "withdrawn"
        f.version += 1
        f.updated_run_id = run.id
        record_event(
            session,
            actor_type="agent",
            actor_id=ACTOR,
            action="finding.withdrawn",
            entity_type="finding",
            entity_id=f.id,
            run_id=run.id,
            before=before,
            after={"status": "withdrawn", "version": f.version},
            rationale="No longer produced by the extraction (thresholds or mappings changed)",
        )
        stats["withdrawn"] += 1
    for d in drafts:
        for to_id, kind, rationale in d.links:
            if to_id in ids:
                session.add(
                    FindingLink(
                        from_finding_id=d.id,
                        to_finding_id=to_id,
                        kind=kind,
                        rationale=rationale,
                        created_by=ACTOR,
                        run_id=run.id,
                    )
                )
                stats["links"] += 1
    session.flush()
    stats.update(
        {
            "findings": len(drafts),
            "voice_of_customer": len(voc),
            "quantitative_metrics": len(met),
            "portfolio_offering": len(eq),
            "level_A": sum(1 for d in drafts if d.evidence_level == "A"),
            "level_B": sum(1 for d in drafts if d.evidence_level == "B"),
            "level_C": sum(1 for d in drafts if d.evidence_level == "C"),
        }
    )
    record_event(
        session,
        actor_type="agent",
        actor_id=ACTOR,
        action="findings.extracted",
        entity_type="vehicle",
        entity_id=f"{vehicle_code}:{market or 'ALL'}",
        run_id=run.id,
        after=dict(stats),
        rationale="Thresholds from config/findings/findings.yaml",
    )
    return dict(stats)

"""Requirement store (Phase 4): import authored requirement files, record PM decisions (gate G2).

Requirements are written as files, ``config/requirements/<vehicle>_<market>.yaml``, by the
requirement agent (offline by the assistant until the LLM API is available, D-055). The import
validates them against the findings, derives the evidence level, upserts with versioning and an
audit event per change. PM decisions are appended to ``config/decisions/requirements.jsonl`` and
replayed after every import, so a rebuilt database keeps them (D-052).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections import Counter
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal

import yaml
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from tracepoint.core.audit import record_event
from tracepoint.core.settings import get_settings
from tracepoint.db.models import Finding, Requirement, RequirementFinding, Run

Market = Literal["EU", "US", "CN", "RoW"]
DECISIONS = {"approve": "approved", "reject": "rejected", "defer": "deferred"}
_LEVELS = "ABCD"


class Criterion(BaseModel):
    market: Market | Literal["ALL"]
    metric: str
    target: str
    method: str
    basis: Literal["evidence", "assumption"]


class FindingRef(BaseModel):
    id: str
    role: Literal["primary", "supporting", "context"] = "primary"


class RequirementSpec(BaseModel):
    id: str
    domain: str
    title: str = Field(max_length=200)
    statement: str
    recommend: bool
    recommend_rationale: str
    horizon: Literal["H1", "H2"]
    horizon_rationale: str
    markets: list[Market] = Field(min_length=1)
    findings: list[FindingRef] = Field(min_length=1)
    criteria: list[Criterion] = Field(min_length=1)
    assumptions: list[str] = []
    uncertainties: list[str] = []


class Exclusion(BaseModel):
    finding: str
    reason: str


class RequirementFile(BaseModel):
    vehicle: str
    market: Market
    author: str
    requirements: list[RequirementSpec]
    excluded: list[Exclusion] = []


def requirements_dir() -> Path:
    return get_settings().config_dir / "requirements"


def decisions_file() -> Path:
    return get_settings().config_dir / "decisions" / "requirements.jsonl"


def _domains() -> set[str]:
    data = yaml.safe_load((get_settings().config_dir / "taxonomy" / "domains.yaml").read_text())
    return set(data["domains"])


def _content(r: Requirement | RequirementSpec, findings: list[dict[str, str]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    domain = r.domain_key if isinstance(r, Requirement) else r.domain
    keys = ("title", "statement", "recommend", "recommend_rationale", "horizon",
            "horizon_rationale", "markets", "assumptions", "uncertainties")
    out = {k: getattr(r, k) for k in keys}
    out["domain"] = domain
    out["criteria"] = (
        r.criteria if isinstance(r, Requirement) else [c.model_dump() for c in r.criteria]
    )
    out["findings"] = findings
    return out


def import_requirement_file(session: Session, run: Run, path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    spec = RequirementFile.model_validate(yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
    prefix = f"REQ-{spec.vehicle}-{spec.market}-"
    domains = _domains()
    errors = []
    ids = [r.id for r in spec.requirements]
    errors += [f"duplicate id {i}" for i, n in Counter(ids).items() if n > 1]
    referenced = {f.id for r in spec.requirements for f in r.findings} | {
        e.finding for e in spec.excluded
    }
    found = {f.id: f for f in session.scalars(select(Finding).where(Finding.id.in_(referenced)))}
    for r in spec.requirements:
        if not r.id.startswith(prefix):
            errors.append(f"{r.id}: id must start with {prefix}")
        if r.domain not in domains:
            errors.append(f"{r.id}: unknown domain {r.domain}")
        for f in r.findings:
            if f.id not in found:
                errors.append(f"{r.id}: unknown finding {f.id}")
            elif found[f.id].status == "withdrawn":
                errors.append(f"{r.id}: finding {f.id} is withdrawn")
    errors += [f"excluded: unknown finding {e.finding}" for e in spec.excluded if e.finding not in found]
    if errors:
        raise ValueError(f"{path.name}: " + "; ".join(errors))

    stats: Counter = Counter()
    for r in spec.requirements:
        links = [{"id": f.id, "role": f.role} for f in r.findings]
        levels = [found[f.id].evidence_level or "D" for f in r.findings if f.role != "context"]
        level = min(levels or ["D"], key=_LEVELS.index)
        payload = _content(r, links)
        existing = session.get(Requirement, r.id)
        if existing is None:
            req = Requirement(
                id=r.id, vehicle_code=spec.vehicle, market_code=spec.market, domain_key=r.domain,
                evidence_level=level, status="proposed", version=1, created_by=spec.author,
                created_run_id=run.id, updated_run_id=run.id,
                **{k: v for k, v in payload.items() if k not in ("domain", "findings")},
            )
            session.add(req)
            record_event(session, actor_type="agent", actor_id=spec.author,
                         action="requirement.created", entity_type="requirement", entity_id=r.id,
                         run_id=run.id, after={**payload, "evidence_level": level},
                         rationale=r.recommend_rationale)
            stats["created"] += 1
        else:
            req = existing
            before = _content(req, [{"id": x.finding_id, "role": x.role} for x in req.findings])
            if before == payload and req.evidence_level == level and req.status != "withdrawn":
                stats["unchanged"] += 1
                continue
            for k, v in payload.items():
                if k not in ("domain", "findings"):
                    setattr(req, k, v)
            req.domain_key, req.evidence_level = r.domain, level
            prev_status, req.status = req.status, "proposed"  # a changed text needs a new G2 decision
            req.version += 1
            req.updated_run_id = run.id
            req.findings.clear()
            record_event(session, actor_type="agent", actor_id=spec.author,
                         action="requirement.updated", entity_type="requirement", entity_id=r.id,
                         run_id=run.id, before={**before, "status": prev_status},
                         after={**payload, "evidence_level": level, "version": req.version},
                         rationale="Requirement file changed; status reset to proposed for G2")
            stats["updated"] += 1
        session.flush()
        req.findings.extend(RequirementFinding(finding_id=f["id"], role=f["role"]) for f in links)
    stale = session.scalars(
        select(Requirement).where(
            Requirement.vehicle_code == spec.vehicle, Requirement.market_code == spec.market,
            Requirement.status != "withdrawn", Requirement.id.notin_(ids),
        )
    ).all()
    for req in stale:
        record_event(session, actor_type="agent", actor_id=spec.author,
                     action="requirement.withdrawn", entity_type="requirement", entity_id=req.id,
                     run_id=run.id, before={"status": req.status}, after={"status": "withdrawn"},
                     rationale="No longer in the requirement file")
        req.status, req.version = "withdrawn", req.version + 1
        stats["withdrawn"] += 1
    if spec.excluded:
        record_event(session, actor_type="agent", actor_id=spec.author,
                     action="requirements.candidates_excluded", entity_type="scope",
                     entity_id=f"{spec.vehicle}:{spec.market}", run_id=run.id,
                     after={"excluded": [e.model_dump() for e in spec.excluded]},
                     rationale="Scope filter: findings that do not become a requirement")
    session.flush()
    stats["requirements"] = len(spec.requirements)
    stats["excluded"] = len(spec.excluded)
    return dict(stats)


def _apply(session: Session, req: Requirement, decision: str, actor: str, note: str,
           run_id: str | None, replayed: bool) -> None:
    before = {"status": req.status, "version": req.version}
    req.status = DECISIONS[decision]
    record_event(session, actor_type="human" if actor.startswith("human:") else "agent",
                 actor_id=actor, action="requirement.decided", entity_type="requirement",
                 entity_id=req.id, run_id=run_id, before=before,
                 after={"status": req.status, "version": req.version, "replayed": replayed},
                 rationale=note)


def decide(session: Session, requirement_id: str, decision: str, *, actor: str, note: str,
           run_id: str | None = None, path: Path | None = None) -> Requirement:
    """Gate G2: approve / reject / defer one version of a requirement and persist the decision."""
    if decision not in DECISIONS:
        raise ValueError(f"decision must be one of {sorted(DECISIONS)}")
    if not note.strip():
        raise ValueError("a decision needs a rationale")
    req = session.get(Requirement, requirement_id)
    if req is None or req.status == "withdrawn":
        raise ValueError(f"unknown or withdrawn requirement {requirement_id}")
    _apply(session, req, decision, actor, note, run_id, replayed=False)
    path = path or decisions_file()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    line = {"id": req.id, "version": req.version, "decision": decision, "actor": actor,
            "note": note, "ts": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
    with path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(json.dumps(line, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    session.flush()
    return req


def replay_decisions(session: Session, run: Run, path: Path | None = None) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Re-apply the committed decisions; a decision only holds for the version it was made on."""
    path = path or decisions_file()
    stats: Counter = Counter()
    if not path.exists():
        return {}
    for raw in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if not raw.strip():
            continue
        d = json.loads(raw)
        req = session.get(Requirement, d["id"])
        if req is None or req.version != d["version"]:
            stats["stale"] += 1  # the requirement changed since; it needs a new decision
        elif req.status != DECISIONS[d["decision"]]:
            _apply(session, req, d["decision"], d["actor"], d["note"], run.id, replayed=True)
            stats["applied"] += 1
        else:
            stats["unchanged"] += 1
    session.flush()
    return dict(stats)


def import_all(session: Session, run: Run) -> dict[str, Any]:
    out: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for path in sorted(requirements_dir().glob("*.yaml")):
        out[path.stem] = import_requirement_file(session, run, path)
    out["decisions"] = replay_decisions(session, run)
    return out
EOF

"""Requirement list exports (deliverable D2): Markdown for reading, CSV for spreadsheets."""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy import case, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from tracepoint.db.models import Finding, Requirement

_LEVEL = case({"A": 0, "B": 1, "C": 2}, value=Requirement.evidence_level, else_=3)


def list_requirements(
    session: Session, vehicle: str | None = None, market: str | None = None,
    include_withdrawn: bool = False,
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    stmt = select(Requirement)
    if vehicle:
        stmt = stmt.where(Requirement.vehicle_code == vehicle)
    if market:
        stmt = stmt.where(Requirement.market_code == market)
    if not include_withdrawn:
        stmt = stmt.where(Requirement.status != "withdrawn")
    rows = session.scalars(
        stmt.order_by(Requirement.priority_score.desc().nulls_last(), _LEVEL, Requirement.id)
    ).all()
    titles = {
        f.id: f.title
        for f in session.scalars(
            select(Finding).where(Finding.id.in_([x.finding_id for r in rows for x in r.findings]))
        )
    }
    return [
        {
            "id": r.id, "vehicle": r.vehicle_code, "market": r.market_code, "domain": r.domain_key,
            "title": r.title, "statement": r.statement, "recommend": r.recommend,
            "recommend_rationale": r.recommend_rationale, "horizon": r.horizon,
            "horizon_rationale": r.horizon_rationale, "markets": r.markets,
            "criteria": r.criteria, "assumptions": r.assumptions,
            "uncertainties": r.uncertainties, "evidence_level": r.evidence_level,
            "priority_score": r.priority_score, "status": r.status, "version": r.version,
            "findings": [
                {"id": x.finding_id, "role": x.role, "title": titles.get(x.finding_id)}
                for x in r.findings
            ],
        }
        for r in rows
    ]


def render_markdown(reqs: list[dict[str, Any]], heading: str) -> str:
    out = [f"# {heading}", "", f"{len(reqs)} requirements. Priority scores follow in Phase 5.", ""]
    for r in reqs:
        out += [
            f"## {r['id']} – {r['title']}",
            "",
            f"*{r['domain']} · {r['horizon']} · markets {', '.join(r['markets'])} · evidence "
            f"{r['evidence_level']} · {'recommended' if r['recommend'] else 'not recommended'} · "
            f"status {r['status']} (v{r['version']})*",
            "",
            r["statement"],
            "",
            f"**Why:** {r['recommend_rationale']}",
            f"**Horizon:** {r['horizon_rationale']}",
            "",
            "| Market | Metric | Target | Method | Basis |",
            "|---|---|---|---|---|",
        ]
        out += [
            f"| {c['market']} | {c['metric']} | {c['target']} | {c['method']} | {c['basis']} |"
            for c in r["criteria"]
        ]
        out += ["", "**Findings:** " + "; ".join(f"`{f['id']}` ({f['role']})" for f in r["findings"])]
        if r["assumptions"]:
            out.append("**Assumptions:** " + "; ".join(r["assumptions"]))
        if r["uncertainties"]:
            out.append("**Uncertainties:** " + "; ".join(r["uncertainties"]))
        out.append("")
    return "\n".join(out)


def render_csv(reqs: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
    buf = io.StringIO()
    w = csv.writer(buf)
    w.writerow(["id", "vehicle", "market", "domain", "title", "statement", "recommend",
                "rationale", "horizon", "horizon_rationale", "markets", "acceptance_criteria",
                "findings", "evidence_level", "priority_score", "assumptions", "uncertainties",
                "status", "version"])
    for r in reqs:
        w.writerow([
            r["id"], r["vehicle"], r["market"], r["domain"], r["title"], r["statement"],
            int(r["recommend"]), r["recommend_rationale"], r["horizon"], r["horizon_rationale"],
            " ".join(r["markets"]),
            " | ".join(f"{c['market']}: {c['metric']} {c['target']} ({c['basis']})" for c in r["criteria"]),
            " ".join(f["id"] for f in r["findings"]), r["evidence_level"], r["priority_score"],
            " | ".join(r["assumptions"]), " | ".join(r["uncertainties"]), r["status"], r["version"],
        ])
    return buf.getvalue()
EOF

import sys
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from tracepoint.db.session import make_engine
from tracepoint.db.models import Finding, FindingLink
veh, mkt = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
with Session(make_engine()) as s:
    fs = s.scalars(select(Finding).where(Finding.vehicle_code==veh, Finding.market_code==mkt, Finding.status!='withdrawn').order_by(Finding.domain_key, Finding.evidence_level, Finding.severity_score.desc().nulls_last())).all()
    links = s.scalars(select(FindingLink)).all()
    lk = {}
    for l in links: lk.setdefault(l.from_finding_id, []).append(f"{l.kind}->{l.to_finding_id.split('-',3)[-1]}")
    for f in fs:
        q = f.quantification
        if f.kind in ("metric_gap","metric_strength"):
            extra = f"score={q.get('score')} peer={q.get('peer_mean')} gap={q.get('gap_vs_peers')} b3={q.get('bottom3_share')}"
        elif f.kind == "equipment_gap":
            items = q.get('catalogue_items', [])
            extra = "items=" + "; ".join(f"{i['item']} {i['price_eur']}EUR std{len(i['standard_on'])}/opt{len(i['optional_on'])}/na{len(i['not_available_on'])}" for i in items[:3])
        else:
            extra = f"c={q.get('complaints')} D{q.get('defects')} U{q.get('difficult_to_use')} W{q.get('wants')} L{q.get('likes')} share={q.get('share_of_market_complaints_pct')}% pt={q.get('by_powertrain')}"
        if f.evidence_level in ('A','B') or f.kind in ('equipment_gap','metric_gap','unmet_need') or (f.severity_score or 0) > 25:
            print(f"{f.id} [{f.evidence_level}] {f.domain_key} {f.kind} sev={f.severity_score} | {extra} | {' '.join(lk.get(f.id,[]))}")
EOF

# Requirements for the BMW 5 Series Sedan (G60), market US.
# Derived from the findings of the G60 US scope by the requirement agent (offline by the
# assistant, D-055). Study scores: US 2025 study, 1-7 derived means; "peer" = mean of the other
# BMW models in the same market (G70). Complaint shares: share of all complaint rows of the
# market (2,625). Targets marked "assumption" are proposals for the PM, not measured values.
vehicle: G60
market: US
author: assistant:claude-opus-5-5
requirements:
  - id: REQ-G60-US-IC-01
    domain: interior_comfort
    title: Front and rear seats comfortable for long drives across body sizes
    statement: >-
      The front seats shall allow a pain-free two-hour drive for drivers from 1.60 m to 1.90 m,
      including a lumbar support that can be set completely flat, and the rear seat cushion and
      backrest shall match the comfort of the front seats.
    recommend: true
    recommend_rationale: >-
      Seats are the largest complaint theme of the interior (62 complaint rows, 2.4 % of all US
      complaints, level A) and both study attributes sit below the peer: front seat comfort
      5.74 vs 6.04, rear seat comfort 5.27 vs 6.24. Verbatims name back pain, firmness and a
      lumbar support that cannot be flattened.
    horizon: H1
    horizon_rationale: Cushion, contour and lumbar calibration change within the life-cycle impulse; no new architecture needed.
    markets: [US]
    findings:
      - {id: FND-G60-US-VOC-seats, role: primary}
      - {id: FND-G60-US-MET-us_2025-seat_comfort, role: supporting}
      - {id: FND-G60-US-MET-us_2025-rear_seat_comfort, role: supporting}
      - {id: REDACTED, role: supporting}
      - {id: FND-G60-US-EQ-seats, role: context}
    criteria:
      - {market: US, metric: Study front seat comfort (1-7), target: ">= 6.0 (today 5.74, peer 6.04)", method: Next US customer study wave, basis: evidence}
      - {market: US, metric: Study rear seat comfort (1-7), target: ">= 6.0 (today 5.27, peer 6.24)", method: Next US customer study wave, basis: evidence}
      - {market: US, metric: Share of seat complaint rows, target: "<= 1.2 % of complaint rows (today 2.4 %)", method: Customer feedback sources A-D, rolling 6 months, basis: assumption}
      - {market: US, metric: Lumbar support travel, target: Can be set to a completely flat position, method: Seat test, basis: evidence}
    assumptions:
      - Study scores of the next wave are comparable with the 2025 wave.
    uncertainties:
      - Comfort perception differs between ICE (71 rows) and BEV (38 rows) buyers; the split is small.

  - id: REQ-G60-US-ID-01
    domain: infotainment_digital
    title: Frequently used functions reachable with one touch or a physical control
    statement: >-
      Climate temperature and fan, seat and steering wheel heating, drive mode, start-stop,
      assistance on/off, volume, map and phone shall each be operable with one touch or a
      physical control while driving, without leaving the current screen.
    recommend: true
    recommend_rationale: >-
      The operating concept is a level-A recurring complaint (53 rows, 39 of them usability) and

from pathlib import Path
p=Path("tracepoint/db/models.py"); s=p.read_text()
a='''    findings: Mapped[list[RequirementFinding]] = relationship(
        back_populates="requirement", cascade="all, delete-orphan"
    )'''

s=s.replace(a,'''    findings: Mapped[list[RequirementFinding]] = relationship(
        back_populates="requirement",
        cascade="all, delete-orphan",
        order_by="RequirementFinding.id",
    )''')
p.write_text(s)
EOF

# Requirements for the BMW 7 Series Sedan (G70), market US.
# Derived from the findings of the G70 US scope by the requirement agent (offline by the
# assistant, D-055). Study scores: US 2025 study, 1-7 derived means; "peer" = mean of the other
# BMW models in the same market (G60). Complaint shares: share of all complaint rows of the
# market. Targets marked "assumption" are proposals for the PM, not measured values.
vehicle: G70
market: US
author: assistant:claude-opus-5-5
requirements:
  - id: REQ-G70-US-IC-01
    domain: interior_comfort
    title: Automatic doors that never open unintentionally while driving
    statement: >-
      The electric doors shall not open from an inside button while the car is moving or a gear
      is engaged, shall start moving within an agreed delay, and shall close reliably from
      outside with a clearly placed button.
    recommend: true
    recommend_rationale: >-
      Automatic doors draw 40 complaint rows (9 defects, 30 usability) next to 45 likes. Several
      owners report that a knee touches the inside button and the door opens while driving: a
      safety risk on a flagship feature.
    horizon: H1
    horizon_rationale: Interlock logic is software; button guard or relocation fits the life-cycle impulse.
    markets: [US]
    findings:
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-automatic_doors, role: primary}
    criteria:
      - {market: US, metric: Door opening from inside button above walking speed or in gear, target: Not possible, method: Function and safety test, basis: evidence}
      - {market: US, metric: Delay from button press to door movement, target: "<= 0.5 s", method: Function test, basis: assumption}
      - {market: US, metric: Automatic door defect rows, target: 0 in the next feedback wave, method: Customer feedback, basis: assumption}

  - id: REQ-G70-US-ID-01
    domain: infotainment_digital
    title: Intuitive controls for a flagship driver
    statement: >-
      The frequently used functions (climate, seat functions, drive mode, start-stop, assistance,
      audio source and volume, navigation zoom) shall be operable with one touch, a physical
      control or a reliable voice command, without searching through apps.
    recommend: true
    recommend_rationale: >-
      The operating concept is the largest digital complaint (66 rows, 62 usability, level A) and
      the study puts controls intuitiveness at 4.36 vs peer 5.20 and controls usability at 4.51 vs
      5.12; touch screen complaints (39 rows, level A) say the same.
    horizon: H1
    horizon_rationale: Software layer and shortcut concept; physical controls in the life-cycle impulse.
    markets: [US]
    findings:
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-operating_concept_operating_system, role: primary}
      - {id: FND-G70-US-MET-us_2025-controls_intuitiveness, role: supporting}
      - {id: REDACTED, role: supporting}
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-touch_screen_operation, role: supporting}
      - {id: REDACTED, role: supporting}
    criteria:
      - {market: US, metric: Study controls intuitiveness (1-7), target: ">= 5.2 (today 4.36, peer 5.20)", method: Next US customer study wave, basis: evidence}
      - {market: US, metric: Study controls usability (1-7), target: ">= 5.1 (today 4.51)", method: Next US customer study wave, basis: evidence}
      - {market: US, metric: Touches for the listed functions while driving, target: "<= 1", method: HMI test protocol, basis: assumption}

  - id: REQ-G70-US-ID-02
    domain: infotainment_digital
    title: In-car connectivity that stays connected
    statement: >-
      The personal eSIM, Wi-Fi hotspot and connected services shall activate once and stay
      working with all major US carriers, including business plans, without repeated resets.
    recommend: true
    recommend_rationale: >-
      Personal eSIM is a large complaint cluster (42 rows, 14 defects) and connected drive /
      infotainment technology is level A (39 rows, 24 defects); Wi-Fi hotspot (4.51 vs 4.98) and
      connected services (4.83 vs 5.13) score below the peer. The rear theatre screen depends on it.
    horizon: H1
    horizon_rationale: Backend, carrier integration and software.
    markets: [US]
    findings:
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-personal_esim, role: primary}
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-connecteddrive_and_infotainment_overall_technolo, role: primary}
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-wifi_hotspot, role: supporting}
      - {id: FND-G70-US-MET-us_2025-wifi_hotspot, role: supporting}
      - {id: FND-G70-US-MET-us_2025-connected_services, role: supporting}
    criteria:
      - {market: US, metric: eSIM activation success on first attempt, target: ">= 98 % across the four largest US carriers", method: Activation logs, basis: assumption}
      - {market: US, metric: Study Wi-Fi hotspot (1-7), target: ">= 5.0 (today 4.51, peer 4.98)", method: Next US customer study wave, basis: evidence}
    uncertainties:
      - Carrier-side provisioning is partly outside BMW's control.

  - id: REQ-G70-US-ID-03
    domain: infotainment_digital
    title: Rear theatre screen usable without blocking the driver's rear view
    statement: >-
      When the rear theatre screen or rear blind is deployed, the driver shall keep a full rear
      view (camera image in the interior mirror or on demand), and the screen shall be easy to
      operate and stream without cables.
    recommend: true
    recommend_rationale: >-
      Rear seat entertainment draws 34 complaint rows next to 20 likes: the lowered screen blocks
      the rear view and streaming often fails; 13 owners explicitly ask for a camera rear-view
      mirror, and rear visibility scores 5.23 vs 5.63.
    horizon: H1
    horizon_rationale: Camera mirror and software fit the life-cycle impulse.
    markets: [US]
    findings:
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-rear_seat_entertainment, role: primary}
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-interior_rearview_mirror, role: supporting}
      - {id: FND-G70-US-MET-us_2025-rear_visibility, role: supporting}
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-rear_view_camera, role: supporting}
    criteria:
      - {market: US, metric: Rear view with theatre screen down, target: Camera image available in the interior mirror, method: Function test, basis: assumption}
      - {market: US, metric: Study rear visibility (1-7), target: ">= 5.6 (today 5.23, peer 5.63)", method: Next US customer study wave, basis: evidence}

  - id: REQ-G70-US-ID-04
    domain: infotainment_digital
    title: Seamless smartphone integration and audio worthy of the flagship
    statement: >-
      Apple CarPlay and Bluetooth shall pair once, connect to the active driver's phone and play
      at the same loudness as native sources; the premium audio systems shall deliver the bass and
      clarity customers expect at this price.
    recommend: true
    recommend_rationale: >-
      Apple CarPlay (28 rows, level A) and pairing (16 rows) complaints match the study gaps in
      smartphone integration (4.79 vs 5.49) and phone pairing (5.03 vs 5.59); audio is level A
      (27 rows) with bass 4.97 vs 5.59 and clarity 5.06 vs 5.68.
    horizon: H1
    horizon_rationale: Software, tuning and speaker placement within the life-cycle impulse.
    markets: [US]
    findings:
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-apple_carplay, role: primary}
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-audio_mode_sound, role: primary}
      - {id: REDACTED, role: supporting}
      - {id: FND-G70-US-MET-us_2025-audio_bass, role: supporting}
      - {id: REDACTED, role: supporting}
    criteria:
      - {market: US, metric: Study smartphone integration (1-7), target: ">= 5.5 (today 4.79, peer 5.49)", method: Next US customer study wave, basis: evidence}
      - {market: US, metric: Study audio bass (1-7), target: ">= 5.6 (today 4.97, peer 5.59)", method: Next US customer study wave, basis: evidence}
      - {market: US, metric: CarPlay audio level vs native sources, target: Within 3 dB at the same volume step, method: Audio test, basis: assumption}

  - id: REQ-G70-US-ID-05
    domain: infotainment_digital
    title: Navigation and voice assistant that get it right the first time
    statement: >-
      Route guidance shall give lane advice early and clearly on multi-lane highways, and the
      voice assistant shall understand natural phrasing of common commands without exact wording.
    recommend: true
    recommend_rationale: >-
      Navigation is level A (28 rows) with the study at 4.85 vs peer 5.53; the personal assistant
      is level A (23 rows) linked to voice recognition (4.76 vs 4.99).
    horizon: H1
    horizon_rationale: Software over the air.
    markets: [US]
    findings:
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-navigation, role: primary}
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-intelligent_personal_assistant, role: primary}
      - {id: FND-G70-US-MET-us_2025-navigation, role: supporting}
      - {id: FND-G70-US-MET-us_2025-voice_recognition, role: supporting}
    criteria:
      - {market: US, metric: Study navigation (1-7), target: ">= 5.5 (today 4.85, peer 5.53)", method: Next US customer study wave, basis: evidence}
      - {market: US, metric: Voice command success on a 50-command natural-language test set, target: ">= 90 %", method: Voice test protocol, basis: assumption}

  - id: REQ-G70-US-IC-02
    domain: interior_comfort
    title: Climate system that cools a large cabin fast and lets passengers direct the air
    statement: >-
      The climate system shall cool the cabin quickly after sun soak, let front and rear occupants
      direct the airflow, and offer temperature and fan controls that do not require menus.
    recommend: true
    recommend_rationale: >-
      Vehicle climatisation (42 rows), blower (23) and air conditioning (20) are all level A; the
      study puts air conditioning performance at 4.48 vs peer 5.19 and climate control at 4.74 vs
      5.14. Owners in hot states describe the car as undriveable for minutes after parking.
    horizon: H1
    horizon_rationale: Vent design and blower calibration in the life-cycle impulse; controls in software.
    markets: [US]
    findings:
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-vehicle_climatization, role: primary}
      - {id: REDACTED, role: supporting}
      - {id: REDACTED, role: supporting}
      - {id: REDACTED, role: supporting}
      - {id: REDACTED, role: supporting}
    criteria:
      - {market: US, metric: Study air conditioning performance (1-7), target: ">= 5.2 (today 4.48, peer 5.19)", method: Next US customer study wave, basis: evidence}
      - {market: US, metric: Cabin cool-down from 60 °C soak to 25 °C, target: "<= 10 min (to be validated)", method: Climate chamber test, basis: assumption}
      - {market: US, metric: Adjustable airflow direction at front vents, target: Yes, method: Design review, basis: evidence}

  - id: REQ-G70-US-IC-03
    domain: interior_comfort
    title: Robust glass roof with an opening option and blinds that work
    statement: >-
      The panoramic glass roof shall not crack in normal use, shall limit heat entry, and an
      opening sunroof shall be offered; the rear and side blinds shall operate by button and
      not get stuck.
    recommend: true
    recommend_rationale: >-
      The panorama glass roof draws 38 complaint rows with 14 defects (cracks, bubbles) and 17
      wishes for an opening roof; sun protection adds 27 rows (blinds stuck, operated only via the
      screen).
    horizon: H2
    horizon_rationale: An opening roof needs a body-in-white change; glass quality and blind fixes start in H1 but the full requirement lands with the successor.
    markets: [US]
    findings:
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-panorama_glass_roof, role: primary}
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-sun_protection, role: supporting}
    criteria:
      - {market: US, metric: Roof glass defect reports, target: 0 cracks without impact, method: Warranty data, basis: assumption}
      - {market: US, metric: Opening sunroof, target: Offered as option, method: Offer check, basis: evidence}
      - {market: US, metric: Blind operation, target: Physical button per blind; no stuck blind in endurance test, method: Function test, basis: assumption}

  - id: REQ-G70-US-PR-01
    domain: powertrain_range_charging
    title: Auto start-stop can be switched off permanently and restarts smoothly
    statement: >-
      The driver shall be able to keep auto start-stop off across drives with one control, the
      engine shall not stop before the car is stationary, and the restart shall not jolt the car.
    recommend: true
    recommend_rationale: >-
      43 complaint rows (28 usability, 13 wishes): the engine stops before standstill, restarts
      with a jolt and can only be avoided in sport mode; drivers describe it as unsafe at
      intersections.
    horizon: H1
    horizon_rationale: Calibration and software.
    markets: [US]
    findings:
      - {id: FND-G70-US-VOC-automatic_engine_start_stop_function_msa, role: primary}
